2021_208_revised_ia_business_officials_m.paragraph: Revised line-item budget worksheet for the International Academy – Okma Campus, prepared for a November 20, 2020 business officials meeting and carried into the Troy Board of Education packet, showing FY20 Final Budget, FY20 Actual, FY21 Proposed, FY21 Midyear, and an FY22 Initial Proposal column. Interdistrict tuition revenue runs from $5,045,395 in the FY20 final budget to $5,667,200 in the FY22 initial proposal, the latter based on 616 students at $9,200, described as 108.23% of the Foundation Allowance assuming no increase. The FY21 Midyear column projects an operating surplus of $268,200 and an ending fund balance of $340,790, or 6.01% of expenditures, while the FY22 Initial Proposal shows an operating deficit of $(67,358). A note records that FY21 expenditures reflect a $294,000 reduction in rent under an approved payment-due-date extension of at least one year.

2021_209_3_a_2021_lease_rfp_docs_ocmw_tr.paragraph: Complete procurement packet for RFP 9929, Professional Office Space Lease for Oakland County Michigan Works! – Troy, operated by Troy School District, covering the cost justification, the RFP document, vendor outreach, bid scoring, and the two submitted proposals. The existing lease at 550 Stephenson Hwy, Suite 400 expires October 31, 2021, and the district sought a five-year lease beginning November 1, 2021 and ending October 31, 2026. L. Mason Capitani scored 95 of 100 points against Friedman Real Estate's 85 and was identified as the highest-scoring, most cost-effective proposal, at $104,916.00 for 2021-22 covering 7,494 square feet at $14.00 per square foot.
2021_209_3_a_2021_lease_rfp_docs_ocmw_tr.page:
**Purpose**
Procurement packet supporting award of RFP 9929, Professional Office Space Lease, Oakland County Michigan Works – Troy Public Schools, presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on September 7, 2021 as item 3.A.

**Need for a new lease**
Troy School District's (Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy) lease at 550 Stephenson Hwy, Suite 400 expires October 31, 2021. The facility requires a 3-5 year lease to maintain operations of what the packet calls the premier One Stop Service Center in Oakland County, serving 17,000+ job seekers and hundreds of area businesses yearly.

**Cost comparison**
Signature Associates assisted with lease cost estimates at no cost to the district, obtaining 2021 quotes for comparable facilities:

| Property | Quote |
|---|---|
| 3221 W. Big Beaver, Troy | $17.00/sq ft + electric |
| 3270 W. Big Beaver Road, Troy | $15.50/sq ft + electric |
| 2855 Coolidge Hwy, Troy | $17.50/sq ft + electric |
| 2800 Livernois Rd, Troy | $17.95/sq ft + electric |
| 850 Stephenson Hwy, Troy | $13.00/sq ft + electric |
| 700 Tower Dr., Troy | $17.95 – 18.95/sq ft + electric |

Moving costs are estimated to average $150,000.00 - $200,000.00, covering technology upgrades, moving servers, build-out of a new facility, moving and packing, furniture, and unexpected costs.

**Solicitation**
RFP 9929 was announced publicly Tuesday, August 3, 2021 via newspaper and the district website, and emailed by Todd Hensley to five area vendors: Robbins Investments 550 LLC (Rob Krochmal), L. Mason Capitani Corfac International (Mason Capitani), Winston-Traitel Realty (Jeff Raitt), Friedman Integrated Real Estate Solutions (Robert Gagniuk), and Thomas Duke Realty (Rachel Pannell). State of Michigan SIGMA VSS/DM added 19 contacts. Proposals were due 1:00 p.m. Wednesday, August 18, 2021 at the Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083. L. Mason Capitani and Friedman Real Estate submitted proposals.

**Lease costs proposed**

| Year | L Mason Capitani | Sq Ft | $/SF | Friedman Real Estate | Sq Ft | $/SF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021-22 | $104,916.00 | 7,494 | $14.00 | $105,000.00 - $150,000.00 | 7,000 - 10,000 | $15.00 |
| 2022-23 | $106,789.50 | 7,494 | $14.25 | $107,100.00 - $153,000.00 | 7,000 - 10000 | $15.30 |
| 2023-24 | $110,536.00 | 7,494 | $14.75 | $109,270.00 - $156,100.00 | 7,000 - 10,000 | $15.61 |
| 2024-25 | $112,410.00 | 7,494 | $15.00 | $111,440.00 - $159,200.00 | 7,000 - 10,000 | $15.92 |
| 2025-26 | $114,283.50 | 7,494 | $15.25 | $113,680.00 - $162,400.00 | 7,000 - 10,000 | $16.24 |

All bid amounts are plus electric and include daily janitorial services; L Mason Capitani costs include maintenance (CAM), while Friedman's are additional.

**Scoring**

| Criterion | L Mason Capitani | Friedman |
|---|---|---|
| Location/Proximity to client Population (50 pts) | 45 | 40 |
| Cost Reasonableness (25 pts) | 25 | 20 |
| Lease Requirements (25 pts) | 25 | 25 |
| Total Points (100 pts) | 95 | 85 |

The review committee comprised Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor; Denise Van Hee, Director – Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy; and Cheryl Schubeck, Program Coordinator. All three scored L Mason Capitani 45/25/25 and Friedman 40/20/25. The district determined L Mason Capitani received the highest evaluation score and is the most reasonable and cost-effective option, with a rate per square foot below current market rates.

**Specifications**
No less than 7,000 and no more than 8,000 square feet; free public parking including at least one handicapped space; public transportation access within walking distance; at least 4 bathrooms; kitchen facility with running water; internet, wireless and telephone accessibility.
2021_209_3_a_2021_lease_rfp_docs_ocmw_tr.verbose:
Full procurement packet for RFP 9929 – Professional Office Space Lease, Oakland County Michigan Works Troy Public Schools, submitted to the Troy School District Board of Education as item 3.A on September 7, 2021. The packet contains four internal sections – Preliminary Lease Cost, Lease Rationale, the RFP itself, and vendor communications – plus the two vendor proposals and SAM.gov registration screenshots.

NEED FOR NEW LEASE. Troy School District's (Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy) lease at 550 Stephenson Hwy, Suite 400 is set to expire on October 31, 2021. The facility needs a 3-5 year lease to maintain operations of what the document describes as the premier One Stop Service Center in Oakland County, providing workforce services to 17,000+ job seekers and hundreds of area businesses on a yearly basis. This identical language appears in both the Preliminary Lease Cost Estimates - 2021 (6 pages) and the Lease Rationale - 2021 (4 pages).

COST REASONABLENESS. Troy School District utilized Signature Associates to assist with lease cost estimates; Signature Associates obtained quotes for comparable facilities at no cost to the district. The 2021 quotes were: 3221 W. Big Beaver, Troy, MI at $17.00/square foot + electric; 3270 W. Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI at $15.50/square foot + electric; 2855 Coolidge Hwy, Troy, MI at $17.50/square foot + electric; 2800 Livernois Rd, Troy, MI at $17.95/square foot + electric; 850 Stephenson Hwy, Troy, MI at $13.00/square foot + electric; and 700 Tower Dr., Troy, MI at $17.95 – 18.95/square foot + electric. Moving costs are estimated to average $150,000.00 - $200,000.00, including technology upgrades, moving servers, build out of a new facility, moving and packing costs, furniture costs, and other unexpected moving-related costs.

SOLICITATION AND OUTREACH. RFP 9929 was announced publicly on Tuesday, August 3, 2021, with a newspaper announcement included in the packet, and posted on www.troy.k12.mi.us. It was sent directly to Robbins Investments 550 LLC – Rob Krochmal, 248-867-3304, robk@surnow.com; L. Mason Capitani Corfac International – Mason Capitani, 248-637-7795, MLCapitani@lmcap.com; Winston-Traitel Realty, Inc – Jeff Raitt, 248-624-7200, jraitt@wtrealty.com; Friedman Integrated Real Estate Solutions – Robert Gagniuk, 248-830-9400, robert.gagniuk@freg.com; and Thomas Duke Realty – Rachel Pannell, 248-476-3700, info@thomasduke.com. The district also used State of Michigan SIGMA VSS/DM, which included an additional 19 contacts. The announcing email, from Hensley, Todd, dated Tuesday, August 3, 2021 at 9:01:04 AM, went to info@thomasduke.com, Robk@surnow.com, MLCapitani@Imcap.com, Greggory.Kent@freg.com and jraitt@wtrealty.com, attaching image001.png and RFP 9929 Oakland County MI Works Office Space.pdf. L. Mason Capitani and Friedman Real Estate submitted proposals by the August 18th, 2021 deadline.

RFP TERMS. Troy Schools accepted firm, sealed proposals to establish a five-year building lease beginning November 1, 2021, extending over a five-year period ending October 31, 2026, annually renewed, containing conditions for termination of the lease without penalty costs or fees should federal funds or other applicable funding sources become unavailable. Proposals and two copies marked "RFP 9929 MI Works Professional Office Space Lease" were due no later than Wednesday, 1:00 p.m., August 18, 2021 at the Purchasing Department, Troy School District, 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083, where bids would be publicly opened and read aloud. Pre-proposal questions were due no later than noon, Wednesday, August 11, 2021, in writing only, faxed to 248.823.4077 or emailed as a Word document to PurchasingOffice@troy.k12.mi.us. The timeline listed RFP Released Tuesday, August 3, 2021; Pre-proposal Questions Due Wednesday, August 11, 2021 @ Noon; Proposals Due Wednesday, August 18, 2021 @ 1:00 PM; Board Award September 2021. Proposals remain firm for a minimum period of 180 days following opening. Section 1.26 states the intent to award at the September 2021 Board of Education meeting, with the contract in the form of a purchase order.

RFP CONDITIONS. Vendors must provide both a sworn and notarized familial disclosure covering any familial relationship between the owner or key employee of the vendor and any member of the Troy Schools Board of Education or the Troy Schools Superintendent, and a completed, sworn and notarized Iran Economic Sanctions affidavit under Michigan Public Act No. 517 of 2012; a false certification carries a civil penalty of not more than $250,000.00 or two (2) times the amount of the contract, whichever is greater, plus investigation costs and reasonable attorney fees, and three (3) years of ineligibility to bid. Section 1.21 requires satisfactory Workers' Compensation coverage and General Liability and Property Damage Insurance of at least $1,000,000.00 per occurrence and $1,000,000.00 in Aggregate, plus automobile insurance of at least $1,000,000.00. Section 1.23 requires certification of non-debarment and registration on www.sam.gov. Section 1.20 permits Troy School District to end the Agreement term upon thirty (30) days written prior notice under a superseding regulatory order. The proposal form requires that the bid not be withdrawn until after forty-five (45) days after receipt of bids, and that the undersigned execute a contract if notified of acceptance within thirty days. Other clauses cover FOIA exposure, survival, incorporation by reference, non-waiver, nondiscrimination, tax-exempt status except for enhancements or additions to real property, standard forms and contracts, and a non-collusion covenant.

SCOPE AND SPECIFICATIONS. Scoring on a 100 point scale used three factors: (a) Location and proximity to client population, 50 points, considering boundaries within the City of Troy, public transportation access and public parking access; (b) Cost Reasonableness, 25 points, reviewing lease changes, annual updates, lease extensions and increases in local government assessments and insurance; (c) Lease requirements, 25 points, covering updates to the property, maintenance responsibilities, upkeep and repair, indemnification, subrogation and related liabilities. Specifications required no less than 7,000 square feet and no more than 8,000 square feet; free public parking including at least one handicapped space; public transportation access within walking distance; at least 4 bathrooms for staff and customers; a kitchen facility with running water; and accessibility to internet, wireless and telephone technology systems. Additional proposal contents included building specifications, a cost proposal with a 2 year cost history of pass-throughs, a proposed schedule of work, and readiness of facility. The proposal form provides blanks for total square feet and lease cost for 2021-22 through 2025-26, plus five references and an exceptions section.

LEASE COSTS SUBMITTED. L Mason Capitani proposed $104,916.00 for 2021-22 on 7,494 square feet at $14.00 per square foot; $106,789.50 for 2022-23 at $14.25; $110,536.00 for 2023-24 at $14.75; $112,410.00 for 2024-25 at $15.00; and $114,283.50 for 2025-26 at $15.25. Friedman Real Estate proposed $105,000.00 - $150,000.00 for 2021-22 on 7,000 - 10,000 square feet at $15.00; $107,100.00 - $153,000.00 for 2022-23 at $15.30; $109,270.00 - $156,100.00 for 2023-24 at $15.61; $111,440.00 - $159,200.00 for 2024-25 at $15.92; and $113,680.00 - $162,400.00 for 2025-26 at $16.24, with a first year of $15.00/sq ft and rates reflecting a 2% annual increase; amortized leasing costs are listed as TBD. All bid amounts are 'plus' electric and include daily janitorial services; L Mason Capitani costs include maintenance (CAM) costs while Friedman's are additional.

SCORING OF BIDS. Location/Proximity to client Population (50 pts): L Mason Capitani 45, Friedman 40. L Mason Capitani was credited with close proximity to a bus stop and two expressways (696 & I-75) and closeness to the Troy/Clawson/Madison Heights population served; Friedman with close proximity to a bus stop and one expressway (I-75) and closeness to the Troy/Rochester Hills population served. Cost Reasonableness (25 pts): L Mason Capitani 25, with an overall rate per square foot of $14 - $15/square ft including maintenance costs described as below market rates and no cost for moving expenses, buildouts or technology; Friedman 20, with a rate of $15 - $16.24/square ft in line with market rates but higher than current costs, maintenance additional, buildout included, and additional expenses for moving and technology. Lease Requirements (25 pts): both 25, each meeting requirements including space, parking, kitchen and bathrooms and permitting lease termination with notice for financial reasons. Total Points (100 pts): L Mason Capitani 95, Friedman 85. Bids were reviewed and scored by a committee of Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor – Troy School District; Denise Van Hee, Director – Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy; and Cheryl Schubeck, Program Coordinator – Oakland County Michigan Works! Troy, with final scores reflecting the average of all three scores in each category; all three scored L Mason Capitani 45/25/25 and Friedman Real Estate 40/20/25. The district determined that L Mason Capitani received the highest evaluation score and is the most reasonable and cost-effective option at this time, with a proposed rate per square foot below current market rates, adding that it would be very costly to move.

FRIEDMAN PROPOSAL DETAIL. The Friedman Integrated Real Estate Solutions lease proposal, dated Aug 18, 2021 and presented by Robert Gagniuk, Real Estate Specialist, Client Solutions (robert.gagniuk@freg.com, 248.848.4093, ECODE 737, cc Anya Eliassen), covers North Troy Corporate Park, 5505 Corporate Drive, Troy, MI 48084, addressed to Denise. Building ownership is Oakland County Health Network (OCHN), which seeks to lease excess office and meeting space to a select network of providers. The lease premises would be +/- 7,000 to 10,000 square feet on the second or third floor; Exhibit A states 2nd floor total available = +/- 23,507 SF and 3rd floor total available = +/- 7,710 SF. Term would commence upon substantial completion with a target date of October 1, 2021, with tenant early entry thirty (30) days prior to install FF&E. 2021_210_2026_tsd_blueprint_world_class_.paragraph: Twenty-slide Troy School District presentation titled "2026 TSD Blueprint – World Class for All," presented September 21, 2021, organizing the district's strategic plan around four color-coded pillars: Green (Early Childhood to Career), Red (Equity and Well-Being), Blue (Deep Learning), and Gold (Building Capacity). The stated mission is "Ensuring learning for all," centering the ONETROY community, with each pillar carrying an overview, objectives and key results. Named targets include applying for 16-32 additional GSRP slots from the State of Michigan in 2021-22 and opening an additional 2-3 PreK classrooms serving 40-60 students.
2021_210_2026_tsd_blueprint_world_class_.page:
**Format**
Twenty-slide PowerPoint, "2026 TSD Blueprint – World Class for All" (Project 2026 Blueprint), on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda for September 21, 2021. Slides 1-3 cover title, Introduction, and Key Themes and Next Steps; slide 19 is a Summary.

**Mission and Vision (Re)Fresh – slide 4**
Troy School District mission: "Ensuring learning for all. Centers ONETROY community." Four framing statements: Early Childhood to Career – expands on research with access through career; Equity and Well-Being – ensures safety, belonging, and connection; Deep Learning – ensures learning for all throughout the system; Building Capacity – expands to include students, staff, and community as learners.

**Core values and accountability – slides 5-6**
World Class for All pillars are described as carefully aligned to core values of Collaboration, Deep Learning, and Focus. The accountability plan holds the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results.

**Green Pillar – Early Childhood to Career (slides 7-9)**
Objectives: continue investing in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for universal preschool for all three- and four-year-olds and access for all; expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students through high-quality career and technical education that expands access to computer science, connects underrepresented students to in-demand careers in high-growth sectors, and builds partnerships with higher education institutions and employers for work-based learning, credentials and college credit.
Key results: apply for 16-32 additional GSRP slots from the State of Michigan in the 2021-22 school year; open an additional 2-3 PreK classrooms (40-60 students) in 2021-22; schedule two meetings and/or site visits with local legislators regarding free preschool for all; building leaders participate in Career Readiness meetings and report back to administrative and building teams twice during 2021-22; the Green Pillar Team researches the Portrait of a Graduate framework during two Career Readiness meetings and develops a Portrait of a Graduate survey by the close of the 2021-22 school year.

**Red Pillar – Equity and Well-Being (slides 10-12)**
Overview: safely reopen schools and support students, particularly those disproportionately impacted by the pandemic; fund additional investments supporting the whole child, including community schools providing wraparound services such as afterschool programs and hiring more counselors, social workers and school psychologists; assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities in all school communities.
Key results: increase social work and counseling support in all buildings; review and monitor student data; emphasize adult learning in well-being and equity; create a common understanding of a system of support at all levels.

**Blue Pillar – Deep Learning (slides 13-15)**
Objectives: create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice; improve technology access for students and families with quality training; pursue global best practices in all content areas; assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities.
Key results: monitor instructional data at least 3 times per year; expand job-embedded coaching; leverage technology for all students in all buildings.

**Gold Pillar – Building Capacity (slides 16-18)**
Objectives: improve educator preparation, strengthen pipelines for underrepresented educators, and support current educators; continue job-embedded professional learning for all staff; provide professional learning for staff, community and students with the goal of co-designing impactful experiences to better the OneTroy community.
Key results: expand hiring networks; expand job-embedded coaching; implement a Delayed Start Model of 90 minutes to ensure collaboration through professional learning, with emphasis on advancing strategic planning priorities; ensure all staff are trained in all departments.
2021_210_2026_tsd_blueprint_world_class_.verbose:
"2026 TSD Blueprint – World Class for All," a twenty-slide PowerPoint template presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on September 21, 2021 under the banner "Project 2026 Blueprint – District School Troy." The deck is organized as an introduction, a mission and vision refresh, a core values and accountability framing, four color-coded pillar sections each with overview, objectives and key results, and a closing summary.

STRUCTURE. Slide 1 carries the title "Project 2026 Blueprint / District / School / Troy." Slide 2 is "Introduction – 2026 Troy School District Blueprint." Slide 3 is "Key Themes and Next Steps – 2026 Troy School District Blueprint." Slide 19 is "Summary – 2026 Troy School District Blueprint," and slide 20 is blank.

MISSION AND VISION (RE)FRESH. Slide 4 states the Troy School District mission as "Ensuring learning for all. Centers ONETROY community," and sets out four framing statements corresponding to the pillars: EARLY CHILDHOOD TO CAREER – expands on research with access through career; EQUITY AND WELL-BEING – ensures safety, belonging, and connection; DEEP LEARNING – ensures learning for all throughout the system; BUILDING CAPACITY – expands to include students, staff, and community as learners.

CORE VALUES AND ACCOUNTABILITY PLAN. Slide 5, headed CORE VALUES, states that the World Class for All pillars are carefully aligned to the district's core values, listing Collaboration, Deep Learning, and Focus. Slide 6, headed ACCOUNTABILITY PLAN, states that the World Class for All pillars hold the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results.

GREEN PILLAR – EARLY CHILDHOOD TO CAREER. Slide 7 introduces the section as covering Overview, Objectives and Key Results. Slide 8 sets the objectives: continue to invest in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for universal preschool for all three and four-year-olds and access for all; and expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students, with a plan aimed at providing more students access to high-quality career and technical education programs that expand access to computer science, connect underrepresented students to careers in demand in high-growth industry sectors, and include partnerships with institutions of higher education, employers and other stakeholders that allow students to engage in quality work-based learning opportunities, earn a credential, and/or earn college credit. Slide 9 lists the key results: apply for 16-32 additional GSRP slots from the State of Michigan in the 2021-22 school year; open an additional 2-3 PreK classrooms (40-60 students) in the 2021-22 school year; schedule two (2) meetings and/or site visits with local legislators regarding free preschool for all during the 2021-22 school year; building leaders will participate in Career Readiness meetings and report back to administrative and building teams two (2) times during the 2021-22 school year; the Green Pillar Team will research the Portrait of a Graduate framework to implement the process in TSD during two (2) Career Readiness meetings; and the Green Pillar Team will develop a Portrait of a Graduate survey by the close of the 2021-22 school year.

RED PILLAR – EQUITY AND WELL-BEING. Slide 10 introduces the section. Slide 11 gives the overview, "Ensuring a focus on Equity and Well-Being": safely reopen schools and support students, particularly those disproportionately impacted by the pandemic; fund additional investments to support the needs of the whole child, including community schools that provide wraparound services like afterschool programs, and hiring more counselors, social workers and school psychologists; and assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities to meet the demands of a world class learning environment in all school communities. Slide 12 lists key results: increase Social Work and Counseling support in all buildings; review and monitor student data; emphasis on adult learning in areas of well-being and equity; and create common understanding of a system of support at all levels.

BLUE PILLAR – DEEP LEARNING. Slide 13 introduces the section. Slide 14 sets the objectives: create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice, with access to deep learning described as imperative for all children; improve technology access for students and families while providing quality training to leverage use of technology to deepen learning; continue to pursue the global best practices of all content areas; and assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities to meet the demands of a world class learning environment in all school communities. Slide 15 lists key results: monitor instructional data at least 3 times per year; expand job-embedded coaching; and leverage technology for all students in all buildings.

GOLD PILLAR – BUILDING CAPACITY. Slide 16 introduces the section. Slide 17, headed "Building Capacity of Students, Staff, and Families," sets the objectives: improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, and supporting current educators; continue to provide job-embedded professional learning experiences for all staff; and provide professional learning opportunities for staff, community, and students with the goal of co-designing impactful experiences to better the OneTroy community. Slide 18 lists key results: expand hiring networks; expand job-embedded coaching; implement a Delayed Start Model to ensure collaboration through professional learning – 90 Minutes, with emphasis on ensuring learning for all staff on advancing strategic planning priorities, citing the Red pillar as an example; and ensure that all staff are trained in all departments.

The deck contains no dollar figures, votes, contract parties or policy numbers; it is a strategic planning framework document.
